name: Daniel Glacier / Southeast Slopes
approach: From the Cathedral Rock/Deception Pass trailhead at the end of FR-4330 (elev. ~3400 ft), start on the signed Deception Pass Trail (also signed Cathedral Pass Trail), which climbs steadily through forest. At about 1.8 miles a signed junction splits off right to Squaw Lake; stay left/straight on the main trail. The trail continues climbing for roughly two more miles, breaking out of trees into subalpine meadows and switchbacks, and tops out at Cathedral Pass (~5500 ft, roughly 4.2-4.5 miles in) at a junction with the Pacific Crest Trail. From the pass, drop briefly toward Deep Lake on the PCT; at a switchback partway down, a use path splits off toward Peggy's Pond, or continue to the signed junction with Peggy's Pond Trail #1375. Either way, the final push to the pond is a rough, primitive 0.5-0.6 mile traverse across narrow ledges with real exposure to steep drop-offs -- go slow here, especially with a pack, and expect it to feel harder than anything on the maintained trail so far. Peggy's Pond (~5,560 ft, about 5-5.5 miles from the trailhead) is the last reliable water and the last established camp; treat water here, since nothing further up is guaranteed. From the pond, braided climbers'/boot paths head northwest and then west across heather benches and talus, gaining roughly 1500 ft over about a mile to reach the broad Southeast Ridge/Slopes of Daniel around 6800-7000 ft. From the ridge crest, the route traverses climbers' trail and open scree below the East Summit (7899 ft) -- faint where it first leaves the ridge, then well-defined -- to a saddle around 7600 ft between the East and Middle Summits. From the saddle, the final few hundred feet to the true (West) summit (7,960 ft) cross a mix of loose talus, lingering snowfields, and the rocky margin of the Daniel Glacier remnant on the mountain's north side. Carry an ice axe and light crampons even in summer -- snow patches here can be firm in the morning and steep enough to want them, and the Daniel/Lynch Glacier ice on the north side opens real crevasses by late summer, so stay on the rock/scree spine rather than wandering onto glacier ice. Hazards worth flagging: an early creek crossing near the trailhead that can be a wet ford in high water, the exposed ledge traverse into Peggy's Pond, loose talus and route-finding uncertainty below the East Summit, and possible lingering snow well into July that can require an ice axe on the approach slopes above the pond.

approach_variants.name: Cathedral Pass, the ledge traverse to Peggy's Pond, and the Southeast Ridge
approach_variants.notes:
From the Cathedral Rock / Deception Pass trailhead at the end of FR-4330, about 3,400 ft, take the signed Deception Pass / Cathedral Pass trail. At about 1.8 miles a signed junction splits right to Squaw Lake — stay left. The trail climbs another two miles into subalpine meadow and switchbacks to Cathedral Pass at about 5,500 ft and 4.2 to 4.5 miles, at the PCT junction.

From the pass drop briefly toward Deep Lake on the PCT; a use path leaves at a switchback toward Peggy's Pond, or continue to the signed Peggy's Pond Trail #1375 junction. Either way the last half mile is a rough, primitive traverse across narrow ledges with real exposure to steep drop-offs. Go slowly with a pack; it feels harder than anything on the maintained trail.

Peggy's Pond at about 5,560 ft, five to five and a half miles in, is the last reliable water and the last established camp.

About 9 km and 2,700 ft.
approach_variants.season: July to September. Snow can linger above the pond well into July and an axe is worth carrying then
hazards: An exposed, primitive ledge traverse into Peggy's Pond, harder than the trail that precedes it
An early creek crossing near the trailhead that can be a wet ford in high water
Loose talus and route-finding uncertainty below the East Summit
Real crevasses opening on the Daniel and Lynch glacier ice on the north side by late summer
Lingering snow into July that can require an axe on the slopes above the pond
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The approach has a hard edge and it is the ledge traverse into Peggy's Pond. That half-mile of narrow ledges with exposure is the last thing between trail and mountain, and it is the point at which a party knows it has left the walking behind. Peggy's Pond is the base camp and the last water.

From the pond, the finding is an altitude and a shape: braided boot paths head northwest then west across heather benches and talus, gaining roughly 1,500 ft over about a mile, to the broad southeast ridge at 6,800 to 7,000 ft. You are on the right ridge when it narrows westward with the Hyas Creek Glacier on your right and Circle Lake far below on your left. That pairing — glacier right, lake left — is the confirmation, and it does not need the summit to be visible.

The next checkpoint is a saddle at about 7,600 ft between the East and Middle summits, reached by traversing climbers' trail and open scree below the East Summit at 7,899 ft. The path is faint where it first leaves the ridge and well defined afterwards, so a faint start is not evidence you are off route.

Where the glacier comes in: to use the Daniel Glacier proper, enter it just north of a prominent spire on the Northeast Ridge and traverse west across it to the Middle Summit.

And the one thing not to do near the top: the true West Summit at 7,960 ft is reached over loose talus, lingering snowfields and the rocky margin of the Daniel Glacier remnant. Stay on the rock and scree spine. Wandering onto the glacier ice on the north side is where the crevasses are.

descent_text: Descend by reversing the ascent line: from the summit area, downclimb the loose scree/talus band beside the Daniel Glacier remnant back to the 7600 ft saddle below the East Summit, then retrace the climbers' trail traversing scree beneath the East Summit back onto the crest of the Southeast Ridge. From there, drop the braided boot paths back down through talus and heather to Peggy's Pond -- in early season, lingering snowfields on this slope offer a quick glissade if conditions allow, but check the runout for rocks first. From Peggy's Pond, carefully reverse the exposed half-mile ledge traverse to regain the Peggy's Pond Trail #1375 junction, then follow the maintained Cathedral Pass/Deception Pass Trail back over Cathedral Pass, past the Squaw Lake junction at 1.8 miles, and down to the Cathedral Rock/Deception Pass trailhead. This is a walk-off/downclimb with no rappelling on the standard line -- rope and rack are not part of a normal ascent or descent here; the only technical gear typically needed is ice axe and crampons for the snow/glacier-margin sections near the top. Some parties climb the Southeast Ridge and descend via the Hyas Creek Glacier drainage instead to avoid crevassed ice on the Daniel/Lynch Glacier side, but that is a variation, not the standard descent. Watch for afternoon softening of any remaining snow on the upper slopes (post-holing risk) and for the same creek-crossing and ledge-traverse hazards from the approach on the way out.
